title: Vanast: Unified Human Animation and Virtual Try-On
summary: Vanast is a single-stage framework that unifies full-body virtual try-on with pose-guided human animation. It generates high-fidelity videos directly from a person's image, garment inputs, and motion sequences, ensuring temporal consistency and identity preservation.
research_notes: Developed by SNU Visual Computing Lab; utilizes a novel synthetic triplet supervision method to train on unpaired data.

evolution.summary: Selected as a CVPR 2026 Highlight, the project formally launched in April 2026. It represents a major shift from disjointed two-stage pipelines to a unified diffusion-based architecture, with public inference code and weights released in May 2026.
